text:
katie-marketing: Hey team — final ask before we lock the launch post: can eng/runtime do a quick sample-shard validation against the marketing benchmark bundle? Need a short smoke that verifies parquet schema, sample coverage, and end-to-end latency numbers (median + p95) for both generation and embeddings. Also want a compare between float vs quantized variants. S3 path: s3://redwood-prod/benchmarks/marketing-launch/2026-03/samples/ . Ideally run on a 1k sample subset and share raw CSVs + a 1-slide summary. EOD PST if possible, thx :pray:

jon-eng-runtime: Ack. We can run a focused smoke sweep. Which model should we target for the slide numbers (redwood-large-v1 by default)? And do you want seq_len capped at 512 or keep real distribution? Also confirm whether we want prefix caching enabled (we can show both cached and cold start).

katie-marketing: @jon-eng-runtime redwood-large-v1 is perfect for the headline. For seq_len please use the real distribution but also provide a controlled run with seq_len=512 for apples-to-apples. And yes — we want a cached vs cold start comparison (very important for the narrative).

maya-eng-runtime: I'll pick this up. Plan: pull a deterministic 1k sample from that S3 prefix (shard selection = first standalone shard), run two sweeps: (A) realistic-distribution, (B) controlled seq_len=512. Both with cached ON/OFF and float32 vs quantized. Command I'll run locally (for reproducibility):

```
# smoke run
tools/bench/run_smoke.sh \
  --s3-path s3://redwood-prod/benchmarks/marketing-launch/2026-03/samples/ \
  --sample 1000 \
  --model redwood-large-v1 \
  --seq-dist observed \
  --controlled-seq 512 \
  --batch 8 \
  --quantized both \
  --cache-modes cold,cached
```

Results and raw CSV will go to gs://bench-results/marketing/1952102468/ (I will mirror to bench-results/1952102468-shard-validate-2026-03.csv). ETA ~3h unless queue spikes.

bench-bot: Job queued: id=jb-20260321-7681, queue position=3. Estimated start 18m.

jon-eng-runtime: quick note — watch out for one gotcha: one of the parquet shards under that prefix historically had mismatched schema (nullable text vs non-nullable). If that shard is picked we should detect and report row counts + any drop. Also trim long context > 8k tokens to avoid OOM in the smoke run.

maya-eng-runtime: Good call. I'll add an explicit schema validation step and a `--truncate 8192` safety flag. Will also output counts: total_rows, dropped_rows, truncated_rows, avg_seq_len.

[~2h later]

maya-eng-runtime: Quick status — first sweep finished, preliminary numbers in the CSV: bench-results/1952102468-shard-validate-2026-03.csv. Short summary: gen median latency (tokens) = 42ms, p95 = 130ms; embed median = 12ms, p95 = 25ms. Float32 vs quantized: quantized gave ~1.8x throughput improvement on gen, but token-level delta ~0.4% (measured on BLEU-ish token overlap). Schema check: no mismatches for the selected shard. Truncated rows = 3 / 1000 (0.3%) because of seq_len cap.

jon-eng-runtime: I inspected the raw CSV quickly — distribution file attached in the bucket. Also ran the cold-start sweep: cold gen p95 = 210ms, cached p95 = 130ms (so caching matters a lot for the narrative).

katie-marketing: This is great — exactly what we needed. Two quick asks: (1) can you produce a single slide-ready table with: sample_count, median_gen, p95_gen, median_embed, p95_embed, quantized_speedup, token_delta, truncated_pct, cached_vs_cold_p95_ratio? (2) can you run one extra cold-only sweep with seq_len forced to 1024 (to show worst-case for users without caching)? If that's heavy, a 200-sample run is fine.

maya-eng-runtime: Will do the slide table and a 200-sample cold-only seq_len=1024 run. ETA for that extra run ~30m.

ryan-product: small note for slides — include a short footnote: "quantized numbers measured on A100-80GB; token deltas measured on held-out 200 samples; caching = prefix KV cache enabled".

bench-bot: Job started: id=jb-20260321-7689 (cold-only, seq=1024, samples=200).

[~25m later]

maya-eng-runtime: Extra run complete. Cold-only seq_len=1024 (200 samples): median_gen tokens = 95ms, p95 = 320ms. I'll add that row to the slide table and upload a PNG of the one-slide summary to the bucket: gs://bench-results/marketing/1952102468/slide-summary.png.

jon-eng-runtime: No schema issues across both runs. Also sanity checked top-5 examples where quantization changed tokens — most were punctuation/tokenizer edge cases.

katie-marketing: Amazing — thank you both. We'll use the float numbers as the primary callout but include quantized tradeoffs in a small callout box. Please drop the CSVs, the slide PNG, and a 1-paragraph methods blurb in the bucket so my comms partner can paste it into the press note. EOD PST still ok?

maya-eng-runtime: All artifacts uploaded: gs://bench-results/marketing/1952102468/{1952102468-shard-validate-2026-03.csv, slide-summary.png, methods.txt}. Methods blurb in methods.txt. Marking this thread resolved unless you want more runs. :white_check_mark:

katie-marketing: Perfect. Closing the loop — will pull the slide and methods. Thanks everyone :tada:
